batchName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476) - Latin words
chapterName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: Rome was still the Urbs Aeterna. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: It was no longer the capital, but still the symbolic heart of the empire.

questions.question: The Goths were settled as foederati. What were they?
options: Allies who kept their own leaders and fought for Rome
questions.explanation: By 395 they were an armed power that could threaten either half of the empire.
questions.sourceQuote: they were settled as allies (*foederati*), peoples who kept their own leaders and fought for Rome in return.

questions.question: Odoacer gave Romulus Augustulus a pension of 6,000 solidi. What were solidi?
questions.explanation: He sent the boy to live with relatives in Campania.
questions.sourceQuote: a yearly pension of 6,000 gold coins (*solidi*)

questions.question: What did Augustulus, the nickname of the last emperor, mean?
questions.explanation: His real name, Romulus Augustus, honoured Rome’s founder and its first emperor.
questions.sourceQuote: rivals mocked him as Romulus Augustulus, “little Augustus”.

questions.question: Stilicho was the West’s magister militum. What was that?
questions.explanation: He fought Alaric at Pollentia and Verona.

questions.question: In 439 the Vandals captured Carthago. Where was it?
questions.explanation: They made it the capital of an independent kingdom with a powerful navy.
questions.sourceQuote: they captured Carthage (*Carthago*), the great port in modern Tunisia

questions.question: In 410 the towns of Britannia were told to see to their own defence. What happened next?
options: No Roman government ever ruled there again
questions.explanation: It was one of many losses as the West shrank.
questions.sourceQuote: In 410 the towns of Britain (*Britannia*) were told to see to their own defence, and no Roman government ever ruled there again.

questions.question: Which river was the Rhenus, crossed by Vandals and Alans into Gaul?
questions.explanation: Perhaps 100,000 people crossed it into Gaul.
